title: Steering detectability: can a model 'notice' it is being steered, and does that break monitoring?

original_idea.body: Train a linear probe to classify steered-vs-unsteered passes; test detectability and correlation with anomalies. Inference-only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain to a forward-looking, deceptive-alignment-adjacent pathway: models reacting to being steered (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probe on steered-vs-unsteered activations; clear methodology, novice+mentor feasible (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (detectability probe + correlation with anomalies), few dependencies (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly forward-looking safety probe on open models (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Linear probing on cached activations, near free-tier (level 5).

novelty.reasoning: Directly grounded in a recent paper detecting steering from within; largely a replication.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Detecting steering from within is already published; this reproduces and extends slightly.
